problem.title: Naturality under non-invertible homomorphisms between same-dimension Weil algebras
problem.user_statement: What about extensions which have Weil algebras of the same dimension? They may be isomorphic, so the method may need to respect some change, that seems to impose extra structure. [Round 0]. Later: Let us therefore go back to the ideas of Round-0, in particular to direction 5 of round 0 with non isomorphic algebras.
problem.current_statement: Round 1 claim (Lilith's single formalized proposal): On the minimal anchor pair A=R[e]/(e^3) (dim 3) and A'=R[e1,e2]/(e1,e2)^2 (dim 3), same dimension but non-isomorphic (dim(m/m^2)=1 for A vs 2 for A'). Generalize Direction 5's isomorphism-equivariance to naturality under EVERY algebra homomorphism between same-dimension Weil algebras (isomorphisms being the invertible special case). Exhibit non-invertible homomorphisms f:A->A', f(e)=e1, and g:A'->A, g(e1)=e^2, g(e2)=0 (noting g is non-canonical -- g(e1)=0,g(e2)=e^2 is an equally valid alternative), each inducing a natural transformation between the associated Weil functors T_A=>T_A' / T_A'=>T_A. Determine whether requiring a method to commute with these induced transformations is (a) a genuinely new, non-vacuous constraint, (b) already implied by existing jet-transport hypotheses, or (c) vacuous/degenerate to only the trivial through-R augmentation-then-unit map.
problem.intent: Test whether same-dimension but non-isomorphic Weil algebras impose any compatibility requirement on a method at all (beyond the trivial through-R map that exists between any two Weil algebras), or whether non-isomorphism genuinely means the two lifts are unrelated and nothing is required -- resolving the complementary case to Direction 5's original isomorphic-algebra framing.

settled_conventions.convention: Per-coordinate Weil lift reading: fix (a-full) -- the full, untruncated, presentation-independent multivariate Taylor expansion of F, evaluated at a W_D-point, with truncation arising automatically from the nilpotency of W_D's generators. Discard (a-trunc) (the literal coordinatewise cutoff at alpha_i <= D_i, shown in Round 3 to be an index-dependent routing rule that deletes W_D-nonzero terms and is not equivalent to (a-full) off the slice). Drop the 'per-output'/index-blind-projection-as-a-second-reading framing as non-local per the user's ruling.
settled_conventions.scope: Definitional convention only -- fixes which construction later rounds on jt-percoord (or its descendants) test. Does NOT itself establish that exact commutation holds for algebraically-presented methods under this convention; that remains an open substantive question MAGI may still test on any future claim that revisits it. Recorded per the user's explicit instruction that this be treated as a convention, not a proven result.
settled_conventions.basis: Round 3 findings (Melchior: (a-full) vs (a-trunc) diverge off-slice, exact witness given; user's own argument: independent per-coordinate symbols tensor to a single Weil algebra, and every Weil algebra is a quotient of a jet algebra, so per-coordinate extension is not a new kind of object under the (a-full) reading).
